limitations: The native ERR_QUARANTINE (a failed submission retired without confirmed loss) needs real driver removal — not forceable on healthy hardware with the shipped artifact; the surrounding guards are pinned and the confirmed-loss release path is pinned by devicelossspec (recorded, not passed).

Pre-existing native defect, NOT fixed (frozen DLL): mixing the real IFileDialog COM dialog with a11y-adapter and Windows-graphics-capture churn in one process sporadically corrupts the native heap (0xC0000374/0xC0000005; minimized reproducers in TRACES.md). The modal-pump test therefore runs on the app's dialog-driver seam (the dialogspec pumpingDriver model) with the real-dialog evidence cited next door; the package's budget is measured stable at four real hosts.
The atlas slot budget (8 process-wide; nothing disposes a window's text-system atlas at close) bounds repeated in-process runs of drawing tests — same budget the a11yspec Narrator note documents.

Real-mode task timers park on the virtual clock (the host does not drive it yet), so a worker parked on Sleep stays unresolved in real mode — the honest record this corpus asserts; the late-completion acceptance is pinned deterministically.

App.Shutdown drains the task layer only (its documented boundary): scope/entity/window teardown rides the window close (WM_DESTROY) and explicit owner calls; effects queued without an update boundary flush at the next App.Update. No orchestrated single-call app teardown was added (out of the bounded slice; the port provides the seams).

The renderer's gate is Renderer.Close, not App.Shutdown: a submission presented after the app shutdown began is still accepted and retires (asserted and recorded in the suite); the app-shutdown -> renderer-close -> host-stop ordering is the application's job (the suite demonstrates the working order).

Bounded native gaps observed from source, not fixed (beyond the slice's minimal-hook discipline): the abandoned frame's native scene handle is not disposed on render.go's error path, and the window's last drawn scene is not disposed at close — the native scene registry grows for the process lifetime (no slot cap); fixing it needs a scene-ownership decision (DrawWindowFrame shares the scene with its caller).

A host-marshaled window query (Alive) issued while a nested modal loop pumps inside a posted foreground closure deadlocks on the wake coalescing — recorded in TRACES.md with the channel-evidence discipline the dialogspec corpus uses.
